title: gating_condition must be an array of full signal UUIDs, not a prose string
description: The `gating_condition` field in signal JSON files is currently a string (or null). In practice it contains partial UUIDs or prose referencing prerequisite signals. Partial UUIDs are ambiguous when signals share a common prefix (as in the sequential `a1000xxx` naming scheme). A prose string is also not machine-checkable: the conductor cannot verify whether gating conditions are satisfied without parsing free-form text. Both problems are resolved by changing the field to a typed array of full UUID strings, making gating unambiguous and automatically verifiable against the signal catalogue before a signal is picked up.
proposed_resolution: 1. Update the signal JSON schema: `gating_condition` changes type from `string | null` to `string[] | null` (array of full UUID strings matching signal_id values in the catalogue, or null if no gate). 2. Update the `fix_signal` tool: before marking a signal as picked up, read its `gating_condition` array and verify each listed UUID has `status: resolved` in the catalogue; if any are unresolved, reject the pick-up with a clear message listing which gates are still open. 3. Migrate all existing signal files that have a non-null string `gating_condition` to the new array format — convert prose references to their corresponding full UUIDs, or to null if the reference cannot be resolved. 4. Update `moeb introspect` (signal a1000042) to emit `gating_condition` as an array in all proposed signal JSON files. 5. Update `spec.skill.md`, `run.skill.md`, and `fix_signal.skill.md` to document the array format with a concrete example.
